messages:
carmen: quick mornings update on radon-12b bring-up (overnight quant sweep). ran int6 + int4 variants against our standard GTN slices. headline: int6 looks safe for most chat loads; int4 saves a lot but introduces some tail latency and a measurable drop on multi-edit/code-rewrite flows. want to propose an intent-aware hybrid canary.

vik: can you share the core numbers and which slices failed?

carmen: from 3k eval (mix of chat, code edits, longform summarization):
- cost per 1M tokens: fp16 baseline = $110 -> int6 = $55 -> int4 = $28
- median throughput (tokens/s): 1700 -> 4200 -> 6100
- p95 short (128 tokens): 310ms -> 280ms -> 330ms (int4 slower due to extra dequant step for short kernels)
- p95 long (2048 tokens): 1.0s -> 1.12s -> 1.53s (int4 has KV pressure + increased fragmentation)
- codegen pass@1 (large code edit slice): 64% -> 62% -> 54% (int4 -10pt vs baseline)
- multi-edit instruction success (small slice ~2.8%): 90% -> 88% -> 79%
- hallucination incidents (free-form summarization): baseline 0.9% -> int6 1.1% -> int4 2.6%

carmen: failing slice is heavily code/structured-edit + iterative feedback (user issues multiple fixes). examples in the audit doc (linked). int4 seems to degrade token-level alignment on small but important control tokens.

samir: do we know if regressions are model quant noise or runtime scheduling? any kernel traces?

carmen: instrumented traces show int4 uses a packed-kv path that increases GC pressure on a subset of hosts. no CPU fallback observed. trace snippet: `runtime: packed_kv_int4 node=radon-12b-ptn-23 mem_kv=1.4GB`

vik: product question: is this likely to be visible to end-users? what's the expected product-level hit if we route aggressively to int4?

carmen: rough product impact model: if we route 60% -> int6, 30% -> int4, 10% -> fp16, blended token cost = 0.6*55 + 0.3*28 + 0.1*110 = 33 + 8.4 + 11 = $52.4 per 1M tokens (~52% saving vs baseline). user-visible: most of quality loss concentrated in ~3% of traffic; we estimate a ~0.03% absolute hit to downstream success metric under immediate fallback behavior.

samir: sounds reasonable. i prefer intent-based routing rather than pure token-length: code-intent -> prefer fp16/int6, chat/QA -> int6/int4. can we use our lightweight intent classifier at edge?

carmen: yes, propose the following routing rule for the canary:
```
routing_v2:
  canary: 5% traffic (split across intents)
  intent_detector: edge_classifier_v3
  rules:
    if intent == "code_edit" or request.tokens > 1500: model = radon-12b-fp16
    elif intent == "multi_step_instruct": model = radon-12b-int6
    else: model = radon-12b-int4
  fallback: if eval_signal.failure >= 2 within 1 session -> promote request to fp16 and record metric
```

vik: SGTM. add per-customer override for enterprise tiers that need 100% fp16. and throttle low-value routes to batch.

carmen: will add opt-out flag. deploy-bot: start canary?

deploy-bot: canary started at 1751012390 - metrics pipeline hooked. canary_id=cnr-17510 status=started

iris-prod: seeing an early p99 tail bump on one host at 1751012422, auto-evicted. observing small spike in KV mem on int4 machines.

samir: action items:
- carmen: finish sample audit + attach canonical failing examples (today)
- vik: wire routing config into runtime feature flag + customer opt-outs (EOD)
- iris-prod: add kernel-specific p99/p999 alarms + eviction runbook (tomorrow)
- samir: set up 72h AB test for two product flows (code-edit & multi-edit) and link dashboards (start when canary hits 5%)

vik: rollback criteria recommendation: if canary increases code-edit failure rate by >3pt or increases product error budget by >0.05% -> rollback to 0%.

carmen: recommendation: proceed with 5% intent-aware canary, use immediate per-session fallback to fp16 on signal, do not global-ship until AB confirms no material regression.

samir: +1. also capture a small cost-benefit table in the canary README for leadership.

vik: ack. please ping when AB dashboards are live. :thumbsup:

carmen: will post audit link and canary README here when ready. thanks all :wave:
